messages:
maya: Heads-up — AcmeCorp (customer id: acme-889) filed a ticket: after completing OIDC SSO onboarding they saw the "account created" success banner but the Console shows NO API keys in the project. They said the UI showed a purple success toast and then an empty list. Ticket ref: SUP-4921.

alex: grabbing the ticket. quick q — was this Dedicated / Private or Hosted?

maya: Hosted. They used the Console flow to provision a default project + API key during first login.

liam: pinging the onboard-bot logs for the provisioning event. can you paste the user's email?

maya: user is rachel@acme.example.

onboard-bot: provisioning_event {
  "event_ts": "2025-11-02T17:12:33Z",
  "user": "rachel@acme.example",
  "flow": "oidc-onboard",
  "project_id": "acme-prod",
  "api_key_id": "key-06a2f3",
  "status": "created",
  "assigned_claim": "proj:acme-staging"
} 

liam: hmm — bot log shows assigned_claim != project_id (proj:acme-staging vs acme-prod). That smells like the tenant-claim race we saw last quarter. When a late background job rebinds project claim the key can exist but not be visible in Console.

alex: can we confirm from the key service (backend) whether key-06a2f3 is bound to proj:acme-staging or prod? liam, can you run the admin lookup?

liam: running admin CLI: 
```
redwood-admin keys get --id key-06a2f3 --json
```
Response: 
```
{
  "id": "key-06a2f3",
  "owner": "account:acme-889",
  "project": "acme-staging",
  "enabled": true,
  "created_at": "2025-11-02T17:12:33Z"
}
```

liam: confirmed — key exists but attached to acme-staging. Console project was acme-prod. So UI doesn't show it because we filter by project.

maya: customer insists they selected "prod" during the onboarding wizard. Is there a chance the flow defaulted to staging because they had a historic sandbox org?

liam: two possibilities: (1) onboarding flow used a cached org claim when the user reauthenticated during OIDC redirect (race), (2) a background provisioning job retried against the wrong project id. I can check orchestrator job logs.

sre-oncall: adding SRE — if we need to rebind the key, we should do a safe server-side update and notify the customer. Rebinding steps: 1) verify usage (no tokens leaked), 2) update key.project -> acme-prod, 3) invalidate previous claim caches. We'll add a short audit entry.

liam: I inspected orchestrator logs — there was a retry at 17:12:35Z with payload project_hint: "acme-staging" from a caching layer. filing internal bug: ORCH-1197.

alex: meanwhile customer needs working keys. maya — can you ask Rachel if they have any live traffic on key-06a2f3 (they probably don't, they couldn't find it). If safe, we can rebind and tell them to generate a new key or we can move it.

maya: asked customer — they confirm no traffic and they'd be OK with us moving the key to prod (they prefer the Console to show the key so their devs can copy it).

liam: performing rebind now. command: 
```
redwood-admin keys update --id key-06a2f3 --project acme-prod --note "rebind after onboarding race SUP-4921"
```
API response: 200 OK 
```
{
  "id": "key-06a2f3",
  "project": "acme-prod",
  "previous_project": "acme-staging",
  "audit": "rebind by liam for SUP-4921"
}
```

sre-oncall: after rebind: invalidate caches — running: 
```
redwood-cache purge --scope project:acme-prod --keys keylist
```
Done.

liam: verifying Console visibility: queried keys list for acme-prod via API: 
```
GET /api/v1/projects/acme-prod/keys  -> returns ["key-06a2f3"]
```

maya: forwarded to Rachel — she confirmed she can now see the API key in Console and copied it. She tested a quick curl and got 200 from the hosted inference endpoint. Example verified: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer key-06a2f3" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/engines/text-gen/outputs -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response 200.

alex: marking ticket SUP-4921 as escalated -> resolved (manual rebind). Opening a follow-up bug to prevent future claim mismatches (ORCH-1197) and adding an onboarding integration test that fails if assigned_claim != project_id.

liam: note for engineering: add a canary that verifies the post-OIDC callback uses the fresh id_token claim (avoid cached org hint). Also add telemetry to detect created keys with mismatched claim/project.

maya: customer thanks the team. leaving a note: set status to "resolved" and add refund note? no billing impact — they hadn't used tokens.

sre-oncall: thumbs up. assigning ORCH-1197 to eng-runtime; tagging devex for onboarding test coverage.

maya: closing the loop: SUP-4921 -> resolved. Thanks all :tada:
